div.head: Nor Grið Lines 1–9

ab.seg: ⁊ on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus
æghwar be mæðe ofer ealle ðam rice.
And on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus cyricfrið and sanctus Wilfriðus and sanctus Iohannes binnan cyricwagum þreo hundred æt cwicum men, and æt deadum botleas.
And oðera stowa grið is læsse mærþe, aa be stowe mæþe.
And preoste cyricgangas syndan forbodene wifum and wæpnum.
And cyricgrið dyre æghwar be mæðe ofer ealle ðam rice.

div.ab: Und im Northumbrer-Recht beträgt [Busse für Verletzung von] Kirchenfrieden des H. Petrus und des H. Wilfrid und des H. Johann innerhalb der Kirchenmauern 3 ‘Hundert’ beim lebend [gebliebenen verletzten] Menschen, und bei getödtetem [ist die That durch Geld] unabbüssbar. Und der Friedensschutz anderer [Kirchen]orte ist von geringerer Ehrenhöhe immer gemäss dem Range des Ortes. Und einem Priester [?] sind Kirchgänge verboten [mit] Weibern und Waffen. Und Kirchen-Friedenschutz schätze [man] hoch überall nach dem Range [der Kirche] über das ganze Reich hin.

And in Northumbrian law [the compensation for breach of] the church-peace of St Peter and of St Wilfrid and of St John within the church walls is 3 ‘hundreds’ for a person [injured but] still living, and for one killed [the deed is] beyond compensation [by money]. And the peace-protection of other [church] places is of lesser dignity, always according to the rank of the place. And for a priest [?] church-goings [with] women and weapons are forbidden. And let [one] value church peace-protection highly everywhere, according to the rank [of the church], throughout the whole kingdom.

ab.seg: And according to the law of the Northumbrians, the compensation owed for a violation of Church sanctuary at Saint Peter’s, Saint Wilfrid’s, and within the walls of Saint John’s is three hundred if the victim is alive, but it cannot be compensated for if he is dead.
And the sanctuary protection of other locations is less in scale, always according to the status of the site.
And a priest is forbidden from attending church with women or weapons.
And Church sanctuary is to be respected everywhere according to its degree over the entire kingdom.

div.note: VIII Atr 1.1; VIII Atr 4; VIII Atr 4.1

Liebermann prints this short text line by line as it stands in its only manuscript, G (Cotton Nero A.i, f. 96v, in a hand of about 1070), and numbers the lines 1–9 (“Zeile”); the dictionary cites it by these lines (“Nor grið Z. 6”). Within the lines he gives, in square brackets, the clause numbers [1]–[4] of the earlier editions; his German translation follows those clauses. Here the whole text is on one page: the manuscript lines are numbered in the margin, and the old clause numbers stand in the text as small grey numbers. A link to one line opens the page with that line highlighted. Rabin’s text and translation are divided into his clauses 1–4, which are the same as the old clauses. Square brackets in the Old English are Liebermann’s supplements (his note 1); most of his readings of the damaged letters come from G. F. Warner (1902).

Manuscripts: G = London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, fol. 96v. Due to an ill-advised attempt by Liebermann to restore a difficult passage in the manuscript using a solution of sulfuric acid, much of the page on which this text appears is now unreadable. Accordingly, editions must now rely heavily on Liebermann’s initial transcription and subsequent reconstruction of illegible words.
Due to damage to the manuscript, this text is based on that found in Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen. Words that have been restored based on Liebermann’s notes are indicated below.
Saint Peter’s, Saint Wilfrid’s, and within the walls of Saint John’s: The three churches specified are those at York, Ripon, and Beverly.
Saint John’s . . . compensated: “John’s,” “hundred,” and “cannot be compensated” are all reconstructed.

Thompson Hydrosulphur freundlich anwendete, mehr als 1901; was mir April 1902 G. F. Warner gütig mittheilte, notire ich dankend.

MS Nero A I f. 96v, after VIII Atr. 5,2, above p. 264 n. 5, hand of c. 1070. Erasures, wear and chemicals make the text partly illegible. When E. M. Thompson kindly applied hydrosulphur, I once saw more than in 1901; what G. F. Warner kindly told me in April 1902 I record with thanks.

Die Hs. lautet Südenglisch und bringt das Stück, laut des Beginnes mit and, als Fortsetzung zu cyricgriðe on Engla lage (VIII Atr. Inscr.; 5, 2); der Text entstand also nicht vor 1014, bewahrt aber Formen noch des frühen XI. Jhs. Der Inhalt kann hinaufdatiren bis c. 933 (das XI. Jh. knüpfte nämlich die Kathedralprivilegien Ripons und Beverleys an Æthelstan’s Schottenzug); allein den Stil beeinflussen Æthelred’s II. Gesetze. Diesen das Stück mit Hs. G als Schluss von VIII Atr. zuzuweisen, verbietet die andere Hs. von VIII Atr. (o. S. 264 Sp. 1), und wohl auch die Ähnlichkeit der §§ 2. 4 mit VIII Atr. 1. 4, 1. 5, 2

The MS reads in Southern English and gives the piece, since it begins with and, as a continuation of cyricgriðe on Engla lage (VIII Atr. Inscr.; 5,2); so the text did not originate before 1014, but still keeps forms of the early 11th century. The content may date back to c. 933 (for the 11th century linked the cathedral privileges of Ripon and Beverley to Æthelstan’s Scottish campaign); but the style is influenced by Æthelred II’s laws. Assigning the piece, as MS G does, to VIII Atr. as its end is ruled out by the other MS of VIII Atr. (above p. 264 col. 1), and probably also by the likeness of §§ 2, 4 to VIII Atr. 1, 4, 1, 5, 2

vgl. Grið 13. Die Unterscheidung, ob Verletzter lebt, fehlt den sonst feiner differenzirten Sonderschutz-Ansprüchen jener drei Dome seit Anfang 12. Jhs., wo als boteles (Hist. of York ed. Raine III 34), Nordisch botalaus (Alured Beverlac. in Raine’s Sanctuar. Dunelm. 1837 p. XV), vielmehr gilt die Verletzung des Asyl verleihenden friðstol, der in Beverley und Hexham noch existirt

cf. Grið 13. The distinction as to whether the injured person survives is absent from the otherwise more finely differentiated claims to special protection made by those three minsters from the beginning of the 12th cent., where what counts as boteles (Hist. of York ed. Raine III 34), Norse botalaus (Alured Beverlac. in Raine’s Sanctuar. Dunelm. 1837 p. XV), is rather the violation of the friðstol conferring asylum, which still exists at Beverley and Hexham
Nor grið 2] Wohl durch gemeinsames Benutzen von VIII Atr 4f. = I Cn 3f. stimmt dies z. T. wörtlich zu Northu 19. Vgl. Gl Kirchenrang 3
[On Nor grið 2] Probably through common use of VIII Atr 4f. = I Cn 3f., this agrees in part word for word with Northu 19. Cf. Gl Kirchenrang 3

Nor grið 3] Eintritt war Weibern untersagt nur zum Altar (Can. Edg. 45) oder zu Cuthberts Reliquien (Sim. Dunelm. ed. Arnold). Im Frankenreiche und in der von Ælfric geschilderten Kirche bedienten Weiber den Priester bei der Messe; vgl. Hirtenbri. Ælfrics ed. Fehr S. xxxvij. 4. 62 = 174. Die Ergänzung ‘Priester’ scheint nötig, denn Bewaffneten oder Ehepaaren stand der Kirchenbesuch frei. Dem Priester verbietet mit Waffen in die Kirche zu kommen Northu 37, Waffen zu tragen manches Zitat Gl Geistliche 29g, aus Ps-Egb. Exc. auch Ælfric ebd. S. xl. 18. 55. 134. 225

[On Nor grið 3] Women were forbidden entry only to the altar (Can. Edg. 45) or to Cuthbert's relics (Sim. Dunelm. ed. Arnold). In the Frankish kingdom and in the church described by Ælfric, women served the priest at mass; cf. Hirtenbri. Ælfrics ed. Fehr p. xxxvij. 4. 62 = 174. The supplement ‘priest’ seems necessary, for armed men or married couples were free to go to church. The priest is forbidden to come into church with weapons by Northu 37, and to bear arms by many a citation in Gl Geistliche 29g, from Ps-Egb. Exc., also Ælfric ibid. p. xl. 18. 55. 134. 225
